_readme: Plan-map data. One entry per topic. Ten-second capture: append {id,title,campaign,status} — wire deps/links later. Viewer: /Aralia/planmap/index.html on any dev server. status: parked | specced | active | done. deps: ids this topic REQUIRES. A dep may also carry `feature: <slug>` to narrow the arrow to ONE feature of the target topic (slug = that feature's title run through the same slugifier as the ids); the `why` still explains the edge, the pointer is now structural. link: repo-relative spec doc path (opened via the dev server's /@fs bridge using repoRoot). Truth-ownership + promotion rules (who owns statuses/decisions/deps; gaps flow UP by human curation only, plan flows DOWN via planmap-to-wave): tools/agora/PLANNING-STACK.md. `open`: integer mirror of the linked subspec's '## Open' bullet count (recompute when the doc changes — it is NOT invented, it is counted). `spike: true`: research that could invalidate the approach (dashed ⚠ tile). status also allows 'superseded' (dead decision — drops to the Graveyard strip; add a one-line `killed` reason). `focus: true` on at most ONE topic = what Remy is actually touching now (★ FOCUS). Freshness fields (2026-07-14 design): `updated` (YYYY-MM-DD, tooling-written date of last real change), `tier` (strategic | component, optional), `status_note` (free-text nuance, topics and features), `decision` (boolean on features: true = waiting on human call).

features.title: Volume ground + GPU fluid: 64m bubble at 25cm, WebGPU compute
features.status_note: ADR 0002. VISUAL PROOF LIVE at design.html?step=water (was ?step=fluid, merged 2026-08-10) (2026-08-06): pour falls, runs downhill in runnels, pools, spills a saddle, levels; 56fps with 2 steps/frame at 256^3; GPU-readback total mass flat with pour off. The scatter kernel RACED (out[neighbor]+= from parallel cells loses mass; WGSL has no float atomics) - rebuilt gather-form: each cell recomputes neighbor outflows and writes only itself; CPU twin fluidGather.ts proves conservation in vitest. Velocity now double-buffered: FIVE buffers, 320MB (ADR said four/256MB). GOTCHA: TSL .mod() emits WGSL mod() which has no i32 overload - use .modInt(); the shader failed silently every frame at 56fps. Open: bubble fill 778ms must move to a worker; wire into live World3D ground; water look REBUILT after Remy rejected v1: shade from true column depth (mass sum), never surface-minus-terrain (25cm quantization noise = checkered mottling); clamp surface to ground+depth; alpha 0 at dry verts kills skirt slivers; fresnel+specular from finite-difference normals; 39fps at 4 steps/frame; still awaits Remy's eyeball; sparse compute restores 64m/12cm for ~100MB when 25cm proves too coarse.

features.title: Water is 2D first: conservative shallow-water solver over a changing bed
features.status_note: ADR 0002 revision 2026-08-07 after a deep research pass. 3D water over the bubble was 16.8M cells at 108ms/step; the same ground in 2D is 65,536 cells and steps in under 16ms measured. Built shallowWater.ts: virtual-pipe fluxes, exact conservation, boundary ledger so water leaving the domain is recorded not deleted, and editBed() that conserves volume when a spell moves the ground. 11 tests. THREE conservation bugs found and fixed: lowering the bed created water, raising it deleted water, and the solver checkerboarded (a cell could shed its whole depth in one step, so cells swapped forever while conserving volume exactly - looked stable for 20k steps).

features.note: Root cause: R3F-mounted scene lights don't drive the WebGPU LightsNode (three #30044 / r3f #2853) -> zero irradiance -> black terrain. Fixed by baking hemisphere+sun Lambert into unlit MeshBasicNodeMaterial colorNodes (no scene lights). Verified on WebGL2-fallback node path; real-GPU eyeball still pending. Sky = fog+CSS backdrop (fine); postprocessing = backlog.

features.title: Probe full-stack parity
features.note: WHY (dep on the material parity pass): parity was proven only on flat terrain + building boxes while the ground world now ships trees, grass, the full prop set, styled roofs, walls/roads/decks. The probe (?phase=webgpuprobe) now renders the SAME full stack the live scene does at the same seed/pose, reusing the game's data (chunk bundles + GroundWorld.props) with the baked-TSL Lambert path. FAIL-FAST aligned with the battle map: pre-checks navigator.gpu + requestAdapter() before mounting; no adapter OR a non-WebGPU backend -> NO scene, an error pane ('WebGPU unavailable: <reason>') with one explicit 'View this scene in WebGL instead' button (routes to ?phase=world3d&ground=1 at the same pose; user-driven, never auto-fallback). Green 'WebGPU' + live FPS badge only on genuine success. Documented MISSING (WebGL-only, shown on-screen): real-time shadows on the node path (no LightsNode consumes a shadow map when lighting is baked into colorNode). Key node-path gotcha found + fixed: on InstancedMesh the InstanceNode multiplies instanceColor into the color pipeline UNCONDITIONALLY, so a dark per-instance scatter tint crushed lit trees/bushes to black — proven in isolation on a real WebGPU backend ([0,19,0] with dark instanceColor vs [109,158,88] without) and fixed by leaving instanceColor null (trees keep geometry leaf-green; bushes use a solid green). Headless capture correctly shows the error pane (no WebGPU adapter in headless Chromium); rendered WebGPU full-stack needs the real-GPU eyeball (RTX 2070S).

Production wanted-watch interactions ask the mounted GroundWorld for the exact player-position crop, current crime records, generated-state standings, matching source settlement defense, and regiment-derived combatants; unsupported static authored towns now enter a structured no-roster source gap with permanent production-shell desktop/mobile proof

Remaining unsupported launchers are explicit no-roster boundaries: static authored-town watch, daily sea encounters, and location-free AI/custom/bestiary simulation each name their distinct missing WorldForge facts and pass permanent production-shell desktop/mobile Vistest proof

HARDEN: make tools/vistest/shoot.ts implement a real --help path and refuse accidental writes to tracked capture directories; the current unknown flag behavior starts the full runner
Register the World Battle Lab as a specialized combat scenario in the canonical visual-test-harness registry and capture runner; do not create a second general-purpose visual harness
DECISION RESOLVED: Road ambush is the first production proving ground because it forces composition, traversal, encounter framing, and source provenance to agree at once.

DECISION: On a world-derived map, must every discrete flower, rock, prop, and landmark be a source-world fact, while only continuous texture/noise/lighting may remain renderer-authored? Recommended: yes.
DECISION: Should missing source semantics fail production scenario parity while remaining visible warnings in the debug lab? Recommended: yes; production must not silently substitute plausible art.

DECISION: Should authored fords remain deterministic difficult terrain at movement cost 2, or add an Athletics check and failure risk? Recommended: keep cost 2 first; add risk only through an explicit traversal action later.
DECISION: Should a destroyed bridge persist as a WorldDelta that removes the Ground deck and invalidates tactical crossing traversal on later visits? Recommended: yes.
DECISION RESOLVED: The next canonical world-battle slice closed the TargetableMapObject gap for source features and props before moving to settlement-edge encounters.

DECISION: Should every prop catalog entry gain explicit fixed/loose mobility and weight facts before Catapult-style spells may select it? Recommended: yes; unknown facts should remain targetable by general object spells but fail restrictive movement filters.

DECISION: Should natural features displaced by roads, plots, and structures be removed or relocated in the shared Local/Ground facts instead of only being suppressed by tactical extraction? Recommended: yes so 3D Ground and combat cannot disagree about stale trees or bushes.

DECISION RESOLVED: Settlement edge and source occupants became the next canonical scenario before deeper object destruction, proving structures, population provenance, deployment, and the real combat UI together.
DECISION RESOLVED: Snapshot resident schedules at combat start and keep those tactical positions stable for the encounter; resample from the world clock after returning to exploration.

DECISION RESOLVED: Settlement-edge defenders come from generated burg, controlling-state, alert, and stationed-regiment facts; becoming enemy actors is a separate explicit-trigger-plus-matching-relation decision.

DECISION RESOLVED: A generated state regiment becomes hostile only when an explicit confrontation trigger and matching player-state relation agree; military presence, wanted status elsewhere, or bad standing without a current confrontation never silently creates enemies.

HARDEN COMPLETE: production wanted-watch fight-in-place encounters provide current witnessed-crime and generated-state standing inputs through the mounted GroundWorld provider; the visual lab fixture remains visibly labeled and is never a production fallback

DECISION: Should hostile generated-state patrols remain limited to one interception per settlement per game day, or should combat outcome, escape, bribes, and standing changes drive a longer event cooldown? Recommended: keep the deterministic daily receipt until those outcomes have authoritative world consequences, then replace cadence with outcome-driven cooldowns.

HARDEN: add mounted-combat and siege-engine object semantics before cavalry or artillery may become tactical representatives; until then retain their exact source counts as visible projection exclusions.

DECISION: Before neutral combat semantics exist, should resident markers be inspect-only identity/activity facts or entirely passive? Recommended: inspect-only, without initiative or targetability, until fleeing, harm, allegiance, and rescue rules are explicit.

Canonical Stream Ford recipe: ford crossings exist in real worlds again (FORD_MAX_RIVER_WIDTH_FT retuned 60 to 225 against the measured 167-1100ft crossing width range; seed 42 now yields 124 fords of 515 crossings), proven by a cell-587 lab preset with stepping-stone paint, 479 passable ford tiles, and a deterministic vistest capture

features.title: RISK: the frozen seedPath determinism contract now exists in two repos
features.note: generateEntityBlueprint imports fnv1a/makeSeedPath/rngFromPath/streamPath from worldforge/seedPath, whose header declares the path-to-seed mapping FROZEN and save-breaking to change. The standalone copied it byte-identical (same sha256). Correct today; the new repo is chartered to build cleaner architecture, and tidying this file silently regenerates every existing character and creature on reintegration. A hash manifest cannot see this. Agora H2.

features.title: RISK: race and class data already forked in the standalone (mocks, 109 vs 116)
features.note: The standalone src/data/races and src/data/classes are hand-typed mocks, not copies. raceMap resolves group = race.baseRace ?? race.id: an unknown id THROWS, but a WRONG baseRace silently selects a different anatomy profile and builds a different body. Agora H3, H4.

features.title: Target boundary found: all Aralia game content collapses to 3 fields
features.note: The engine reads only race.name/cls.name (label), race.baseRace ?? race.id (anatomy group), and a CLASSES_DATA existence check. So ~29 KB of D&D content becomes SpeciesRef{id,name,baseRace?} + ArchetypeRef{id,name}. The engine needs a species registry the HOST injects, not D&D data. Deleting src/data/** from the standalone removes the mock and the fork at the root. Agora H4.

features.title: BLOCKER for the remote: CC-BY assets committed under a bare MIT license
features.note: The standalone tracks 21 files / 30 MB in public/ (base meshes + clips), carries MIT, and has NO CREDITS file. The base meshes are CC-BY 4.0 and require attribution. Already in git history, so a late fix means a history rewrite. Must be settled BEFORE the remote and visibility decision. Agora H5.

features.status_note: Remy approved 2026-09-27 ("also rivers and water flowing in rivers"); the bar is real river video (q29: the Merced, the Nerang, a stream close-up). Round 1 (2026-09-28) built a momentum shallow-water solver over a seeded judged reach (src/systems/world3d/river/, solved once in a worker), a two-phase flow-map water material, and a bed and bank material; open it at ?step=water&river=1; doc docs/architecture/domains/world3d-river-water.md. Drawn speeds match the model within 4% except the slow pool. Blind judges: round 1 LOST (the white water reads as flat decals, the rocks as gray eggs on top of the water). Not yet in the game: the in-game ribbons need a flow map per river course. Round 5 (2026-09-28) was a variant round: the white slabs fixed, then V1 rock contact, V2 white water placed by the flow, V3 depth and direction, V4 stones and wet margins, V5 = V2 + V3. All eight judgments lost at high confidence, and every judge named the same four gaps whatever the lever, so round 6 ships them together, with the white water rebuilt as see-through streaks and Remy's width, depth and flow controls. WebGPU (2026-09-30, Remy: "can we move this to webGPU?"): the scene draws with three's WebGPURenderer and TSL node materials, the ocean's renderer, with no WebGL path (the one water, GG-341); the five judged frames differ from WebGL only by filter and rounding (0.6 to 25.6 % of pixels over 8/255, each pair looked at); the WebGPU frame is CPU-bound on three 0.172 (16.9 against 11.0 ms at bank-along, GG-362), and the three 0.172 workarounds are listed in GG-363 and GG-364. Live headwaters expansion (2026-10-04): a 70 m mountain-cliff waterfall feeds the plunge pool, rapids and diverging main/offshoot channels. Falling water uses discharge divided by opening area, gravity, stream thinning, low-flow drips and impact spray, with river refraction and lighting. The same discharge enters the solver at the landing patch; the cliff is excluded from the shallow-water solve. Pool initialization now follows its sill rather than multiplying its full depth with flow. The drop menu adds rubber duckies, rowboats, sticks, branches, scattered individual leaves and expiring foam with different drafts and drag responses. Camera following moved into a dropdown for the paper boat and individual drops; independent below-ground/below-water permissions and a solver-bed/rock inspection overlay are available. Main-branch editing and settled branch-flow calibration remain future work. See docs/architecture/domains/world3d-river-water.md. Existing local Design Preview wiring remains ignored. Yosemite and Merced realism gauntlet (2026-10-04) remains active: independent rendered reviews still reject the falling-body breakup and source cliff/contact. Shared measured landing state now unifies renderer and solver. Its width 1, depth 2, Q 1.5 run passed three balanced 60-second windows after 1860 simulated seconds, zero restores and negligible mass residual. This is numerical evidence, not a realism pass or real-river calibration. Original downstream optics remain the preservation baseline.

features.title: River floaters: a paper boat and a few ducks carried by the river's flow
features.status_note: Remy asked 2026-09-28: a paper boat floating down the river (a test of the flow and the buoyancy), and ducks that paddle different ways while the flow plainly carries them. Added to rivers round 4, after its flow work. The boat relaxes to the surface velocity, spins with half the local curl, bobs on the drawn waves, slides round rocks, runs aground in shallow water, and starts again upstream; a "Pin camera to the paper boat" button follows it. Each duck's ground velocity is its paddle plus the current, with its body facing its paddle heading, so the crab angle shows the carry. Proof: the boat's speed against the surface speed, each duck's ground minus water velocity against its paddle, and motion strips. Procedural mallards for now; Savi's Tidewrack mallards can swap in later with Remy's download OK.

features.title: River controls: sliders for the river's width, depth and flow in the river scene
features.status_note: Remy asked 2026-09-28: "in the river flow, i'd like to get some controls on the rivers width and depth, is it possible to make a UI that let's me control the river?" A panel in step=water&river=1 with sliders for channel width, channel depth and flow (the discharge), because the three are tied (flow = width x depth x mean speed); the mean speed and Froude number show live. On release the reach rebuilds (bed, banks, low-water thread, the seeded rock field scaled to the channel, the flow field and the surface); the paper boat and the ducks carry on in the new flow; Reset river returns the shipped values; the panel is hidden in captures, so the judged frames do not change. Routed to the rivers builder for round 5 step 2. BUILT 2026-09-29 by the ocean gauntlet lead (Remy: "i don't see the controls to change the river shape?"): the River shape panel under the camera buttons, with width x0.6 to x1.6, depth x0.5 to x2 and flow 0.5 to 12 m3/s; a release rebuilds the reach and solves its flow (22 s for one step); the camera stays; the mean speed, depth, Froude number and wet area show; Reset river; &rw= &rd= &rq= in the address. The default draws the judged river bit for bit (riverShape.test.ts). Checked in headless Chrome at a slider step and at two extremes. See the domain doc world3d-river-water.md. LIVE since 2026-09-29 (the live river editor): in a browser the sliders act while dragged, as bed patches over the judged reach; the rebuild on release now runs only in a static page (a capture or &live=0).

features.title: Live river editor: grab the river and reshape it live, with the flow running live
features.status_note: Remy asked 2026-09-29: "make it so i can grab the river and i can manipulate the river shape live, without reloading". BUILT 2026-09-29. In a browser the river scene (?step=water&river=1) runs its solver live in a worker, and a second worker turns the running field into flow maps about 4 times a second; the captures keep the steady field (0 px over 8/255 against a baseline, with and without the cache). An edit is a BED PATCH over the judged reach: the ground, the rocks, the stones, the plants and the solver's bed change in place near the change, and the water keeps flowing and fills the new shape (the front reaches a moved bend in 0.3 s and fills it by 20 s). The River shape sliders act while dragged (width 3.1, depth 3.4, flow 14.8 updates a second). The EDIT MODE (the panel's "Edit the river's path" button; Esc leaves) puts blue path handles on the course line's control points (a drag moves the river's path: 4.9 updates a second, 182 ms a round trip) and amber bank handles (a drag widens or narrows the channel there: 9.7 a second, 68 ms). &rc= keeps the edit in the address; Top up refills a drained pool at once. The design s keeps the pools and the sill in place when a point moves. Limits measured: the solver held in every extreme; a channel pushed against the grid edge spills past its wet ceiling and shows the mesh seam. Code: riverLive.ts, riverMapWorker.ts, riverEditHandles.ts, riverLiveClient.ts. Doc: docs/architecture/domains/world3d-river-water.md, "The live river editor". NODE HEIGHTS (Remy 2026-09-29: "make it so that i can make the river nodes be able to go up and down individually"), BUILT 2026-09-29. Each control point has a green height handle beside its path handle (drag up or down, -3 to +5 m, 1 cm steps; its label names the height in meters and what it does to the water; "Reset height" per point, "Reset river" for all; &rc=...h9:-1.58). The bed follows a smoothstep between points (no overshoot, local to the neighbors) and a mound over the middle 70 % of the channel, so a large raise is a dry hump with a side channel on each side. A raised stretch gets an edited design level: a minimax flood finds the pass over it, and the water ponds upstream to the pass + 0.2 m. Each patch reports each point as deeper, shallower (a riffle), split (a dry hump, water goes round) or block (a pond that spills over the pass, with its side and length), and the panel shows the water that edits took or added and warns of water at the grid edge (GG-342 and GG-343 reported, not fixed). Measured: point 9 -1.5 m deepens the middle from 0.60 to 1.84 m; point 17 +2 m makes it 0.59 m from 1.15 m; point 17 +4.5 m stands 2.98 m over a 2.45 m bank with the water 6.5 m wide beside it; point 9 +1.6 m ponds 25 m and spills over the right side at 3.55 m, 0 breach cells at 90 s of flow. Height drags: 7.3 to 9.8 updates a second, 57 to 115 ms a round trip. A heights-only patch copies the judged outside fields, so a height changes the ground only under its mound. The judged frames stay 0 px (max 0, no cache). Tests: riverNodeHeight.test.ts (12). Open: GG-349 (the pass flood sees only the band), GG-350 (the fields refresh cut moves the ground up to about 1 cm on a course or width edit), GG-351 (the mound shape is fixed); GLOBAL_GAPS.

features.title: Skip stones: throw a stone at calm water and see whether it skips, by throw angle, tilt, spin and stone type
features.status_note: Remy asked 2026-09-28: "a modal where i can throw rocks into the water, and see if it will or wont skip based on angle of the throw and the type of rock". A Skip stones view in the Design Preview water window, on a calm lake sea state in the ocean viewer. Controls: stone type (flat slate, round pebble, thick chunk, pumice that floats, clay disc), speed, flight angle, tilt, spin, release height; presets for the best throw and for throws that fail on purpose. Physics from Clanet, Hersen and Bocquet (Nature, 2004: a best tilt near 20 degrees, a closing window of flight angles, a minimum speed) and Rosellini et al. (J. Fluid Mech., 2005: lift on the immersed area, loss per bounce); spin keeps the tilt steady. Each touch leaves a splash and ripple rings, and a readout says why the stone sank. One water means one depth and flow state for the whole map, fed by rain and springs, run down the world's river network into lakes and the sea; the FFT waves as detail on top where the water is deep and open, fading in shallow water and against a river's current; one look that reads depth, speed, silt and foam; one foam field (GG-291); one water ledger; one renderer. features.title: Depth read never reaches the screen: 37.2 m of water draws the same pale cyan as a 10 cm film, so a filled hole reads as a skin
features.note: Remy 2026-08-25. The sheet IS rendered (__waterDebug: compiled, 114,456 indices, surface 36.5 m above ground top) — his "not rendered" hypothesis was disproved. Shader math is right: 1-exp(-37*1.1) saturates, so it must resolve to deep #194654. Switching the preset to sea darkens it immediately, proving the color tracks the SHALLOW endpoint. Two depth-blind suspects named, not isolated: constant emissive (waterLook.ts:123, intensity 0.22) and a hemisphere light at 5.0 (PreviewVolumeGround.tsx:3052). The Daylight slider separates them — emissive survives darkness, scene light does not. NOTE the page opens on ocean skin + pond, not sandbox. FIXED 2026-08-28: the cause was the studio rig (hemisphere 5.0 + constant fills 2.3 and 0.5 against a 2.6 sun key), not the emissive. Proven by dropping the hemisphere to 0.4. Fixed by scaling indirect light on the water material only, so the judged ground look is untouched. Named "Puddle-deep lake" in the Water Hall of Shame.

features.title: See-through water and light on the bed: refraction through the surface, caustics on the floor
features.note: Remy picked all three halves in round four. Built as a THIRD look beside sandbox and ocean skin: refraction needs a different material class, so folding it into either would change a judged look. Seeing INTO it uses three own transmission with one change — three treats thickness as one number for the whole material, and for a lake the right value is the surface-to-bed distance. The sheet already carries that per vertex, so the transmission chunk is hand-expanded and its thickness line repointed at it. Caustics ported from the battle map, weighted to the shallows because caustics are light that reached the bottom. FOUR faults found and fixed, all by capture: the albedo painted depth a second time on top of Beer law (near-black lake); the absorption distance was 3.2 m on water five metres and deeper, which makes a transmitting surface look identical to a non-transmitting one (Hall of Shame 15); a pale self-lit emissive tuned for an opaque surface washed over the refracted scene; and transmission replaces alpha blending, so the shallow fringe drew solid until thin water was dropped outright below 3 cm. THE FINDING THAT MATTERS BEYOND THIS LOOK: on the same 44,331 m3 lake, the two judged looks draw 9.9 percent of the frame as water and this one draws 23-34 percent. Their opacity ramps start at 0.14 at the shore and most of a lake AREA is shallow, so from overhead a large lake is nearly invisible in both. Open: reflections of sky and shore.

features.title: Ripples driven by their causes: twenty-three signatures, two of them derived
features.note: Remy picked seven in round 3, six more in round 4, and all ten of the next batch in round 5 — so the list grew by his choice rather than by curation. Each carries size, strength, decay and repeat, argued from what the event physically IS rather than tuned by eye, because eye-tuning failed twice: rain came out thirty times too hard, and a spell reached 10.9 m because repeated pushes at ONE cell resonate. Six causes LIFT the surface (wind, bubbles, boil, swimmer, surfacing, partWater) and a test names them, so a dropped minus sign still fails. TWO ARE DERIVED and nobody places them: rapids where the Froude number is high, and the hydraulic jump where it CROSSES one — a two-cell test, not a threshold, because a uniformly supercritical field is all rapids and no jump. The deck groups them by behaviour: press once, keep running, and the solver finds these. 24 unit tests.

features.title: Frame water button: point the camera at the water, and say when it is down a shaft
features.note: Aims at the depth-weighted centre of the whole wet set, sized by its spread, and always above the terrain — a camera placed relative to the WATER ended up inside the hillside. Reports "sunk N m below the land" when the pool is under the rim, which is the honest answer on the sandbox cell.

features.title: Liquid skin for the land droplets: a screen-space fluid surface, written for WebGL2
features.note: Remy called the droplets ugly, and on this page they were THREE.Points sprites — so you saw balls. Now they are drawn as spheres into a depth buffer, that depth is smoothed with a narrow-range filter, and the result is shaded as a surface. Written for WebGL2: flipSurfaceRender.ts does the same job in TSL on three/webgpu and none of its code carries across. The ground is drawn depth-only into the same targets, so terrain occludes the water without a copy of the scene. Sprites stay one click away on the same water. Three faults found and fixed, all by looking rather than by measuring: a linear colour written straight to the screen (black lumps), a filter sized in pixels for a subject sized in metres (2 m droplets projecting to 58 px against a 12 px kernel), and a one-pixel checkerboard from a per-pixel choice between forward and backward differences. Hall of Shame entries 12, 13 and 14. Open: refraction, and a performance reading.

features.title: See-through water is the DEFAULT, and it only costs when there is water
features.note: Remy round 5 q16 chose it; round 6 q18 asked to stop paying for it on frames with no water, and round 6 q17 confirmed the PHYSICAL read is what he wants — shallow water shows the bed. The cost is three own transmission pass, a second render of the opaque scene, which it runs whenever a visible un-culled object carries transmission. So the frame loop hides the sheet when its draw range is zero, and recomputes the bounding sphere so frustum culling can answer the in-frame half honestly. No material swaps class per frame. The measurement that settled q17: on the SAME 210,368 pixels, sandbox reads rgb(40,87,99) at 60 percent saturation and see-through reads rgb(79,84,74) at 12 percent, passing about twice the red — which is the lake bed, visible through six metres of water. The older looks go opaque within two metres, so they call almost any water deep. One is stylised, one is physical, and Remy picked physical.

Remy 2026-10-29: water must react to the land, and spells change the land, so the world has ONE ground record (groundRecord.ts): the ground height grid plus ordered shape-ground world deltas. Step 1 done: the record, saved edits replayed at build, the live river bed reads its fine grid and takes live edits. Step 2 done: the drawn terrain and roads take every edit (fine patch per edit, paving cut away), WebGL and WebGPU. Step 3 done and proven live 2026-10-30: in a real in-place fight Mold Earth (excavate) and Fireball (crater = the 3D arena sphere) cut the world ground and both holes showed in the exploration view; four blockers fixed (handoff lost to StrictMode cleanup, in-scene casts never resolved, record facts lost in the world-gen worker copy, crater classifier never fired for real abilities). 2026-10-30: the fight-in-place view now streams the real town (its own chunk loader; exploration disposed the handed-over one), follows the game clock and draws the generated bodies; a saved crater survived a full page reload. Open: trees, props, buildings, static water and built volume bubbles do not follow an edit; Move Earth and Wall of Stone need a form and line choice; holes read near-black.
